title: A full chant
hook: the day a kid plays the whole song, not just the chorus: homage, refuges and precepts, start to finish
tomorrow: a month of Pali. what did it actually give you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the other great languages: dhamma and dharma, nibbana and nirvana, namo and nam mo. Two spellings, one word. Today, every word of the chant, in order.
screen: `TWO SPELLINGS, ONE WORD.` → `EVERY WORD, IN ORDER.`

segments.voice: There's a day when a kid who has only ever played the chorus on guitar plays the whole song, first verse to last chord, without stopping. Nothing new gets learned that day. The stringing together is what's new. Weeks of Pali come to that today: the homage, the refuges and the five trainings, start to finish. And with it comes the fear that rides along with leading anything out loud: what if I lose my place?
screen: `NOT JUST THE CHORUS.` → `THE WHOLE SONG.` → `WHAT IF I LOSE MY PLACE?`

segments.voice: Strung together, the chant has three movements. First, the bow: namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammasambuddhassa. Homage to him, the Blessed One, the worthy one, the fully awake. Said three times. Second, where you stand: Buddham saranam gacchami, dhammam saranam gacchami, sangham saranam gacchami. To the Buddha, the teaching and the community, I go for refuge. Then the set again, dutiyampi, a second time, and tatiyampi, a third. Third, how you'll walk: five trainings, each with the same ending, veramani sikkhapadam samadiyami, I undertake the training to refrain. From taking life. From taking what isn't given. From sexual misconduct. From false speech. From drink and drugs that cloud the mind into carelessness. Notice the order. It doesn't open with rules. It opens by honoring someone, then by saying where you shelter, and only then by saying how you'll live. In a temple, a monk may lead it line by line while the room answers, which is how kids learn it, half a beat behind. And if you lose your place, the shape finds it for you: bow, refuge, training. Namo, saranam, sikkhapada, pieces from this block, clicking together. The whole chant.
screen: `THE BOW: NAMO TASSA, THREE TIMES.` · `REFUGE: BUDDHAM, DHAMMAM, SANGHAM.` · `THE TRAINING: FIVE, ONE ENDING.` · `LOST? FIND THE SHAPE.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE CHANT.`

segments.voice: Chant the whole set from the screen at an easy pace: the homage three times, the refuges three times, then the five trainings. If you lose your place, don't start over; find the shape and step back in. Then sit in the quiet it leaves.
screen: `NAMO TASSA BHAGAVATO ARAHATO SAMMASAMBUDDHASSA (×3)` · `BUDDHAM SARANAM GACCHAMI · DHAMMAM SARANAM GACCHAMI · SANGHAM SARANAM GACCHAMI` · `DUTIYAMPI … TATIYAMPI …` · `PANATIPATA · ADINNADANA · KAMESU MICCHACARA · MUSAVADA · SURAMERAYAMAJJAPAMADATTHANA — VERAMANI SIKKHAPADAM SAMADIYAMI`

segments.voice: A full chant: homage, refuges and the five trainings, start to finish. A bow, a shelter, a way to walk.
Your line: the whole chant. Bow, refuge, training, and the shape will hold your place. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: At Theravada temples, lay people may begin a visit or a ceremony by chanting the homage, taking the three refuges and the five precepts, repeating each line after a monk who leads.

fork.setup: a seven-year-old in the temple class asks why she has to promise not to drink beer. what's a fair answer from the chant itself?
options: she has to, or she isn't a real Buddhist.
it's a training she takes up, samadiyami, about keeping a clear mind.
the fifth line is only for grownups, so she can skip it.
fork.reveal: samadiyami: I undertake. the precepts are trainings taken on, not laws handed down, and the fifth is about what clouds the mind into carelessness.

original.note: Pali, in Devanagari letters: to the Buddha I go for refuge, the first line of the refuges.

trapdoor: what you thought: a long string of Pali to get through.
what it means: three movements, a bow (homage ×3), a shelter (refuges ×3) and a way to walk (five trainings, each 'I undertake the training to refrain').
what a scholar hears: the order puts honor and refuge before conduct, and samadiyami makes the precepts self-undertaken trainings rather than commands.
guess: homage, refuges and the five trainings, chanted start to finish
every discourse in the Pali canon, sung on one night
a long chant monks sing alone at the close of the day

chat.says: the Lao kids' teacher wants me to lead the whole chant sunday. i always lose my place at the precepts.
options: Hold the shape: homage, refuges three times, five trainings. Each one ends samadiyami.
Memorize it as one long sound. Thinking about the meaning is what trips you up.
Skip the precepts part. The homage and refuges are the only lines that count.
chat.meaning: The full chant has a shape: homage, refuges three times, five trainings that end veramani sikkhapadam samadiyami. The shape finds her place.

sikkhapadam.meaning: a training rule, a step of training
